utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. This is case number IT-03-67-PT, the Prosecutor versus Vojislav Seselj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Today is the 2nd of May, 2007. Good morning to everybody. Good morning to the representatives of Madam Prosecutor. Good morning, Mr. Seselj. And good morning to all the people helping us in this courtroom. Good morning, in particular, to the interpreters. As you know, today is our third Status Conference. Before dealing with the points I plan to speak to today, I will ask for appearances because I can see that Mr. Saxon is not with us today. So I would like to meet those who represent the OTP today. Please, the appearances.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: May it please the Court, my name is Christine Dahl, I am a new senior trial attorney on the case. With me today is Sanja Bokulic and Ulrich Mussemeyer and Klaus Hoffman.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, thank you, Madam. Let me greet you since you are the senior trial attorney in charge of the case as of now. Today, I shall first endeavour to meet the various points raised last time by Mr. Seselj before I turn to other subjects. Mr. Seselj, last time you raised a host of issues, and since then I have had various, several, working meetings with the registry in order to try and find answers to those questions. At the last Status Conference, you raised the fact that allegedly in the United States $70.000 would have been seized and supposedly they belong to you. I put the question to the registry. I wondered whether it was not the registry that had done this or whether there was a Judge in this Tribunal that would have issued an order for this bank account to be frozen. I received an official answer from the registry. To their knowledge, nothing was done by this Tribunal; therefore, this action could only have been carried out within the framework of something external to this Tribunal. It may have been done by the European Union or by the USA, but then, if so, if there was something done from outside the Tribunal, you must have been informed of it. You know that when assets are frozen, the holder of the account is informed, at the very least by his or her bank, or by the authority requesting the measure. Therefore, you should normally know who blocked your accounts. You had those accounts in the United States, but please know that this did not come from this Tribunal, not from the registry, not from a Judge who would have ordered your account to be frozen. So this is what I'm able to tell you on this issue. If you want to take the floor, I will gladly allow you to speak; otherwise, I'll move to another topic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Antonetti, it is, indeed, quite possible that there is no formal decision on freezing that bank account; but as you know, in the West there is a widespread practice of making informal decisions in the wings which may have far-reaching consequences. There are two things that I find very symptomatic. Firstly, the account is frozen after I have informed the registry in writing that I was a holder of that account. I handed over to the registry all the information and all of my assets and property; after that, the account was frozen. Secondly, I have it in writing from the American Consulate here in the Netherlands, a certificate that the money was seized. This was given to the Serbian consul in The Hague at his insistence…. and there were no legal grounds for seizure; with a clause that I could use the money solely to pay the American lawyer who would defend me before the Hague Tribunal. I can bring this to the following Status Conference. I can have it sent to you, whichever way you like. There is a document like that in English, and that is a fact. Therefore, I am talking about two facts. I never said I had this document from the registry formally requesting that. As you know, decisions have been made by both the American authorities and the European Union to block the bank accounts of all fugitives from justice indicted by the Hague Tribunal, but there is no decision to block or freeze the accounts of those indicted before the Tribunal, especially since this money is from 1989, and that is before the war every broke out. I wanted to use part of the money for paying for my defence, but the money has been seized, the assets have been frozen, and I have nothing else to say except if perhaps you want me to have that document forwarded to you for you to see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much for the explanation. Second issue you raised last time. You said that at the first Status Conference, the conference had not been broadcast to your country so that many people were deprived of watching the Status Conference. I was quite concerned about this because if what you'd been -- what you'd said was true, that would be intolerable. I was told the following by the registry: As you know, this Status Conference is being filmed by cameras; that's the reason why you have cameras all around the courtroom. However, the actual broadcasting outside of this courtroom can happen in two ways. First, it can go through the web site of the Tribunal, through the internet, where you have the three courtrooms that are scheduled, and somebody who's outside who wants to follow the proceedings can click on the courtroom he or she is interested in to have both sound and image. And then there is an NGO, Domovina, which takes it upon itself to broadcast various excerpts. I was told by the registry that, as far as they were concerned, they did not put any obstacle to having the Status Conference broadcast. And if there was any problem, it must have been a technical problem, and so far the registry could not explain the source of the problem. But they promised to look into the matter. And I will keep you informed as soon as I know what the technical problem was. However, regarding this non-government organisation in charge of broadcasting various passages filmed in the courtroom, there I have no power. So this is what I wanted to tell you regarding this issue you raised last time, and you quite rightly raised last time. Third point, you mentioned it was something to do with the cell and the adjacent cell in which you would be allowed to inspect your documents also during night-time. The registry told me they had looked into the matter from all angles, and that it had appeared that there was a technical problem; namely, that the wall separating your cell from the one next to yours - that could be used as a library by you - was 1 metre wide. I will go and see you, as I promised. I will go and see you on site very soon. I can't check now whether it is, indeed, 1 metre wide; but if it is so, well, of course one will have to break through the wall to make an opening, and 1 metre -- well, you'll need some kind of mechanical equipment to do it. So this question has been put to the technical services of the registry, but to date I have not been told of any further developments. Here again, as soon as possible, you will be informed. But I was led to believe that so far you can only access in the middle of the night, you can't -- you cannot access this other room, which can cause problem for you. Do you have anything to say to this, about this cell come library?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Mr. Antonetti. I've already said everything that I had to say about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. You had raised another issue, that of interpretation and translation. With regard to translation issues, I met with the service in charge of translation, and CLSS conveyed the following to me by way of information: This service has currently 24 people who translate documents from B/C/S into English, and it has 14 staff members working from English into B/C/S or into other languages. But all of the staff members have to work on all the cases before this Tribunal. There is no special team assigned to your case. But this -- the odd 30 people can, depending on various priorities, translate immediately some documents, provided some priority is explained to them. I also asked how long it took for a translator to translate a given amount of pages. The following has been said to me: If one has to translate four pages, you need one translator a day. So one translator can only translate four pages. But once the translation has been done, revision comes into play; in other words, the translator who has done the translation is going to pass on the document to somebody else who is going to check the translation. In other words, when you, yourself, file a request for 40 pages, say, it means that the translator will need ten days to translate the document. Obviously, based on priorities, several translators can be assigned to the job at any given time. Based on this figure, you can imagine all the problems that may arise in terms of deadlines. Something else was said to me. There are many pages waiting to be translated. CLSS does its best for the parties and the Trial Chamber to be able to receive translations in due time, but they cannot do more than what they can, given the means they have received. At any rate, one thing is very useful for all, it is to know that to translate four pages, you need one translator working one day. This is a very relevant point which had to be conveyed to you, because last time you had explained to me that you wanted, needed, to be able to read judgements by the International Tribunal for Rwanda and that you had to resort to private translators, since CLSS had not been able to provide you with the judgements in their translation. Therefore, if you want to be made aware of the way the translation service operates, there is a document in English. I'm not aware whether it exists in B/C/S, but it may exist in B/C/S. It is a practice direction on the translation services of the registry. This document explains, sets out the way the service operates, how priorities are established; it may be of use to you. I will ask the registry to send a copy to you very shortly so that you be informed of the way the translation service operates. It is a practice direction that was adopted on the 16th of November, 2006. So this was regarding translation matters. Last time, you raised the issue of 40 folders that you did not want to receive. They are, in part, connected of course with a decision by the Appeals Chamber issued recently regarding disclosure in electronic format. I'll come back to this later, but I wish to speak with you about the contents of the 40 folders because I received a list. They're not 40 folders, there are exactly 38 of them. So I pondered and I asked myself what they might be inside those folders. There is a first part, folders 1 to 10, and they include documents relating to witnesses scheduled by the Prosecutor. So these are folders -- folders by witness. There is an alphabetical list: AB, BC, CD, DE, EG, KL, MN, V -- VZ. So all in all, you have ten folders. Among them, I found out that you had the prior statements by the witnesses, and most of the time they were in English and had not been translated into B/C/S, which of course is going to raise a problem because they would have to be translated into your language. But there are other folders including translations into B/C/S. So you have ten folders concerning witnesses which are scheduled to appear. Folders 11 and 12 concern expert witnesses: Ewa Tabeau, Oberschall, Riedlmayer and Stankovic. All the expert witnesses are to be found in these two folders, and there again I noted that there were transcripts in English, apparently without translation. Folder 13 includes documents, six of them, which have to do with judicial notice. Apparently, they are in English and B/C/S, so there'll be no problem there. Folder 14 is an important one for you because it contains, under Rule 68 of the Rules, anything that can be exculpatory. There's a CD-ROM; I don't know what's on it. There's a document entitled "What is Proposed by the Serbs," and then there are other documents. I'm not going to go into the details of the documents, but they may be extremely relevant for you. Folders 15, 16, and 17 contain documents relating to the Krajisnik testimony which he did during his trial. These are transcripts in English, not in your language. Folders 18, 19, and 20 are judgements following judicial notice. So there are three folders. Folders 21 contains testimonies of 15 witnesses who seem to be spread between your case and Slobodan Milosevic's case. So there would be 15 statements or testimony. Some are in English, not translated. Folder 22, this concerned another witness: Reynaud Theunens. Folder 23 concerns two other witnesses. Folder 24 is made up of various witnesses who testified in other trials, but who mentioned your name; as a result, you have their witness statements. So this is for folder 24. Folder 25, you will find in this folder transcripts of various hearings under 65 ter, but they are in English, not in B/C/S. Folder 26 contains Prosecution's requests and applications from 2003 to 2006. Folder 27 also deals with the requests or applications; they are all in English. Folder 28 deals with the counsel who had been assigned as a stand-by counsel; everything is in English. Folder 29, decisions from 2003 to 2006 by -- issued by Trial Chamber II probably. As to folders 30 and 31, oddly enough they contain legal documents: memos on points of law, joint criminal enterprise, the lack of bias of Judges, protective measures, a series of documents - of legal documents that is - that are to be found in folder 31. Folder 32, it relates to Witness VR017, same -- it also concerns him in the following folder. Folder 34 contains transcripts of the Simic trial. Folder 35, transcript of the Simic trial in English. Folder 36, you find various documents, administrative or otherwise. Folder 37 contains documents regarding other witnesses. And lastly, you have a folder containing transcripts of the Milosevic trial and other documents. So here you have the 38 folders or binders. So now what is Mr. Seselj's situation? These binders are very important for you. You can go about them in two ways, but you may yourself be of a different view. Let me tell you how you could do -- tell me -- let me tell you about the two ways, and then you will convey to me your standpoint. So for now, the 38 binders are in possession of the registry. The first solution would be as follows: As soon ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As soon as you have your three assistants or associates in addition to Ms. Regus, the registry will take the 38 binders to the Detention Unit and you, assisted by your associates and Ms. Regus, you could sort the documents contained therein in order to select those that seem necessary, indispensable, to you. So that could be one solution. The second solution would be the following: Since the Prosecution has transmitted and disclosed under Article 68 a certain number of documents to counsel, then I could request from Prosecution to transmit to you officially these documents. Those are two ways we could deal with the matter and which would enable us to solve the question, besides the other item of disclosure, which I will talk a bit later. So on these points, Mr. Seselj, do you have now a position, a very clear-cut position, concerning these 38 binders?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Antonetti. David Hooper was never my attorney. His material are not materials of my defence. From this survey of yours, it was my understanding that most of his material consists of documents he received from the Prosecution. Sometimes, perhaps, some of these documents may have been submitted to me as well. I don't know which ones were and which ones weren't, but handing documents over to David Hooper is not handing them over to my Defence. I suggest that you either burn them completely, all these documents, or return them to the Prosecution. I'm not interested at all in whether David Hooper did something for my Defence and whether he got some confidential information, whether he obtained something fundamental and whether this can be disclosed to the Prosecution or not. I'm not interested in that at all. I am very happy to say right now that David Hooper can join the Prosecution against me. I will never receive David Hooper's materials. I will receive all the materials submitted to me in a proper way - on paper and in the Serbian language - from the Prosecution, from the Trial Chamber, from the registry. I have been perfectly clear on that. From this we can see, Mr. Antonetti, that a vast amount of material has never actually been handed over to me, especially not in accordance with Rule 66 and even more so in accordance with Rule 68. I'm grateful to you on a precious bit of information that you gave to me just now. You confirmed that Hooper several times on my behalf, without my knowledge and approval, met up with the Prosecution in accordance with 65 ter and that there are records of such meetings. This is proof, as far as I'm concerned, that he was an instrument of the Prosecution because if he attended such meetings without my consent, that means that he had the consent of the Prosecution. So this is what I really find precious. I would like to have these records but in the Serbian language. However, I'm not going to take them from Hooper. I insist that the Prosecution provide me with them in the Serbian language so that I have yet an additional argument to prove that the proceedings against me are irregular and certainly cannot be just. As for disclosure, you said that that problem would be examined later during this Status Conference, so I am going to deal with this in a substantive matter later on when you put it on the agenda. As far as Hooper is concerned, I think that things are quite clear. Also, my legal advisors are not going to take over his material, we're not going to look at it, we are not going to leaf through it. It simply does not exist for us. What exists for us is only what I received through official channels. Every time I sign receipt of each and every document. I never refused to sign for receiving a particular document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So your position is now perfectly clear and I am now going to ask Prosecution's position, ask the Prosecution what its position is. I have listed a while ago the 38 binders and their contents, and obviously it seems clear that a certain number of documents must be transmitted to the accused under Article 68 or under Article 66. You have actually satisfied this obligation by transmitting a great number of documents to the counsel who had been designated and which the accused voiced protest and contested the appointments. So these documents have never been seen or received by the accused because he received -- he refused to receive them and he hasn't received them. So he challenged this. Without entering into details, taking the binders concerning witnesses whose name start by A and B, several witnesses therefore, and the statements, written statements of these witnesses or documents which may have been attached to the written statements, were transmitted in English in these binders and transmitted to counsel. Therefore, in theory, the accused has no knowledge of these documents. Also, in the same way, in the case of binder 14, some documents have been transmitted or communicated under Article 68. The accused have never seen them and they are -- since they have been transmitted, they have remained in the binder without the accused having knowledge of them. So taking into account two decisions made by the Appeals Chamber and the fact that the accused may defend himself - and I'll come back also on the question of the electronic disclosure - it appears that Prosecution should transmit to the accused the documents under Article 66 and 68 as provided for in the Rules. So who would in the Prosecution team answer, give its position on this question?

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. It appears that Professor Seselj may not be aware of the most recent decision of the Appeals Chamber of 17 April 2007, in which the Chamber approved the electronic form of disclosure. I say this because --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I will talk about this in a moment, so then you will have all the elements. Concerning electronic disclosure -- you may sit down. I will give you the floor later. The Appeals Chamber made on the 17th of April, 2007, a decision, according to which the Appeals Chamber confirms the position of Trial Chamber I, which had decided that the documents could be disclosed in the electronic form. The Appeals Chamber then reminded -- recorded the fact that it was for the Chambers to exercise their discretionary power recognised by case law of the Appeals Chamber, that this discretionary power, which is recognised to the Chambers, should be examined possibly under the angle of manifest error which could cause a prejudice to the accused. The Chamber recalls that in the case of a discernible mistake, each Chamber has a discretionary power, except in the case of a discernible error. Chamber -- Trial Chamber I has -- Trial Chamber I committed a discernible mistake, the Appeals Chamber answers no. Inasmuch as Trial Chamber I had indicated in its decision that disclosure would be done by the electronic way inasmuch as the accused would have had at the time a counsel. Therefore, the Appeals Chamber rightly so concluded that there had been no mistake by the Trial Chamber I which would have allowed after that to give a favourable answer to the request of appeal certification performed by the accused. This being said - and this is very important - the Appeals Chamber decided -- wanted to specify in its decision in paragraph 20 -- I shall read slowly paragraph 20 which will be translated in Mr. Seselj's language. I quote, and this will also be translated in English, paragraph 20, which is fundamental: "This being so, the Appeals Chamber remarks, observes, that if it doesn't conclude in the present decision that the Impugned Decision had a mistake, contained a valuation mistake, nothing prevents it -- nothing prevents Vojislav Seselj to request an amendment of the decision to the Trial Chamber newly seized of the case, which Chamber could, indeed, decide exerting its powers to follow a different approach concerning management of the proceedings." Therefore, the Appeals Chamber rejected appeal of the accused, but invited the accused to make a new request, to formulate a new request, so that he may in the future -- he may have in hard copy the documents provided for under Article 68 and 66. Therefore, Mr. Seselj, I think I understood last time, but I'd like you to tell me again today, you are requesting, therefore, from the new Trial Chamber, for which I am the Pre-Trial Judge and for which I have the power under Article 73 to decide on this matter, to disclose to you in the future all documents under Article 66 or 68 in hard copy.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Antonetti, I can submit a request to you orally to review the decision made by the previous Trial Chamber, and my legal advisors can also write this up and they will probably do so. I have already received the ruling of the Appeals Chamber dated the 17th of April with a few days of delay because of the translation. I can't remember the exact date when I received it, but the date is registered in the registry. In all legal systems, there is a possibility for the body in charge, according to standard procedure, that is to say in a legal way, pass a decision that cannot be carried through. For example, the Trial Chamber can pass a decision that I have to stand on my head throughout the proceedings in this courtroom. That decision cannot be carried through. The Trial Chamber can also decide that I receive all documents in the Chinese language; theoretically that is possible but it is undoable. It is equally undoable to pass a decision that I receive documents in electronic form. I do not use a computer. I do not use this form. I'm never going to use a computer. I'm an old-fashioned man. I write everything in my own hand, with my own pen, and every day I write about ten pages or so. Your translators need an entire working day to translate four pages, and I write more than ten pages and one of my pages is like two journalist's pages. Now, what happens? The Trial Chamber is before an obvious dilemma. They are either going to renew this decision to have everything disclosed to me in electronic form and then the proceedings will take place without my participation. I will sit in the courtroom quietly. You are all going to hear these witnesses, and I will just sit there quietly, and you are going to pass your judgement. That is one solution. I'm prepared for that. You see, my basic motive is that I strictly abide by legal principles and that I be remembered in the history of international law and justice in that way. There is another solution that your standpoint presented at the first Status Conference, Mr. Antonetti, in accordance with what you decided together with your colleagues from the Chamber, that you re-examine the old decision and look at a new one, making it incumbent upon the OTP to deliver all documents to me in writing, on paper, and in the Serbian language. I fully commiserate with the suffering of the registry in terms of translation. If they have 30 translators, let them employ 300 translators. It is not really my problem. It's not something that has to do with me and that I have to resolve it; it's the problem of this Court. If you do not have enough translators, if you have 30, then employ 300. If 300 is not enough, make it a thousand. You could have done all of that within these four years -- four years and three months at that. They could have done all of this, and they did nothing about it. Why not? Because they were quite sure, they in the OTP and they in the registry, that I would have counsel imposed on me, that I would not have a right to my own defence, and that then they could do whatever they wanted to do. Now, all of these documents have piled up, and I insist that I receive all the documents involved, and I'm going to wait for another four years. Perhaps I'm going to wait for another 14 years. I don't think that I'll be waiting for another 40 years, I don't think I'd live to see that. But I'll wait for another 14 years or whatever it takes. I came here to wait, didn't I? I'm not displaying any kind of impatience. They are impatient. They want to get a judgement as soon as possible without doing anything. I am just so patient. Look, the years have been going by and I've been patiently waiting. I hope that I will live to see the day that they meet all their obligations vis-a-vis the Trial Chamber and vis-a-vis myself. Mr. Antonetti, the Office of the Prosecutor on the 6th of November - you probably have this - submitted a review of all material that was disclosed to me according to Rules 66 and 68 and a list of material that I rejected because they were in electronic form or in the English language; that is why I refused to receive them. On the basis of this, I infer that there is a vast body of material that has not been disclosed to me at all. It's perhaps 200.000 or 300.000 only in accordance with Rule 68, and I insist that I receive all of this because the OTP has to bear in mind that Rule 66 and Rule 68 have equal legal force. You cannot do what the Prosecutor would like to do, and that is to push forth and give priority to Rule 66, while disregarding Rule 68, where, by definition, the Prosecutor is an officer of international justice. He has an equal obligation to find exculpatory material and incriminatory material. Their obligations are the same on both scores, but obviously no one has persuaded the OTP of this so far. Also, I insist that I receive the transcripts of all testimonies of all witnesses in all proceedings, all of those who mentioned my name at least once during the course of their testimony. I submitted that request - when was it? - three years ago, whatever. The Trial Chamber instructed the OTP to hand this over to me, but they haven't done so yet. Then they tried to evade this responsibility and then they said, He doesn't need the testimony of witnesses related to Kosovo because that is not part of his indictment. I need all of this, though. Look at the Milosevic case, the Milutinovic et al case, look at Kosovo where my name was mentioned in a false context. I am proving in this way my thesis regarding the instrumentalisation of false witnesses. A witness there mentioned Seselj's paramilitary formations and there absolutely weren't any; and then there are some Muslim witness who are talking about Seselj's White Eagles, which is contradicto in adjecto. It is absolutely impossible. And in this way, I am refuting the basic thesis of the Prosecution. Therefore, I insist on all of this. As for Rule 66, since the Prosecution has professional witnesses who have appeared in several cases, I insist that I be given the statements of all these witnesses, also the interviews conducted by the investigators with these witnesses, and all their statements -- rather, all their testimonies, including cross-examination, on paper in the Serbian language because I reckon it is easiest for me to catch them out when they lie. They testify in one case and they mention my name, then they appear in my case, and then they accuse me of the same things that they accused other people of previously. That is very important for my defence. Without the assistance of the OTP, I cannot do this efficiently. The Prosecution has to put all of this on paper and have it translated into the Serbian language, if you want to have a serious trial. You know there is this intention on the part of the OTP to shorten trials. In the Milosevic trial, Geoffrey Nice twice stated explicitly that he wants all the remaining witnesses to be treated as 92 bis witnesses, and he even invented another thing - you can find this in the transcript - he even invented Rule 92 bis and a half as a rule for saving time, but time cannot be saved in contravention of the interests of justice. The interests of justice are more important than saving time here. You waited for four years? I'll wait for another four years. I'll wait for you. Translate all of this into the Serbian language, put it all on paper, and the trial can start. Without that, I do not see how the trial can start.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Well, I am now going to ask the Prosecution. The situation is the following. Mr. Seselj has just presented his request. He had already done so several times with his arguments. He announced that his legal counsel would address soon a request so that the decision of the Appeals Chamber may be applied so that the present Chamber, for which I am the Pre-Trial Judge under Article 73 and for which I have all powers, should reverse its decision and quash completely the decision. So as soon as I will have received this written request, Prosecution will answer, of course, and I will then give out my decision. Of course you can imagine what sort of decision I will probably be led to take, but one has to respect the procedure. As from the decision which I will have made, there may be on the Prosecution's side, if the Prosecution has not followed a request for certification of the appeal and the Appeals Chamber might then have to say whether my decision has no manifest discernible error resulting in prejudice for the accused. But looking at matters more serenely, the following assumption, the accused should have in hard copy in his own language all the documents provided for under Article 66 and 68. For the moment, I do not know exactly what -- how far the situation reaches, what is the extent of the situation. I suppose that took -- during the years which have passed, the accused will have received some documents in English and in B/C/S, but that it happened, I think in particular in the months before the opening of the trial, that the Prosecution transmitted to counsel the documents in question. And therefore, there is a real problem; that is to say that the accused has not received all the documents provided for under Article 66 and 68. Since now the situation is the following, the accused is defending himself without counsel, which means that normally if my decision goes this way, the trajectory of the documents, the direction of the documents, will be from Prosecution to the accused directly without any intermediary or counsel. So I suppose that the Prosecution is going to review all the documents and verify all this and it's going to take a certain time. But today, is the Prosecution in a position to give us some clarifications on this matter?

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Your Honour, in preparation for handling this case, I studied carefully the two prior transcripts of the Status Conferences this Court has held. We will endeavour to make information available in a manner that is accessible to Professor Seselj that is consistent with the practice of the Tribunal and the need to serve the interests of justice expeditiously and avoiding unnecessary work. There is a matter here of disagreement regarding Professor Seselj's assertion that he has not received material. When he says he has not received material, what he means, in fact, is that he has rejected it. He has wilfully blinded himself because he does not like the form and the content of the material because it is not to his liking. There is a fundamental disagreement with whether or not Mr. Seselj uses a computer. Prior to turning himself in to the Tribunal's jurisdiction and arriving in The Hague in 2003, Professor Seselj publicly announced that while in the Detention Unit in Scheveningen, he would be using his laptop to write books. And if I may, Your Honour, play a video-clip of the interview with a journalist from February 2003. This was produced by BK Telecom. I'm going to play first the introduction where the journalist welcomes Professor Seselj to the studio, and then I will switch to the portion in which the journalist asks Mr. Seselj what he will be doing with his time while in detention. The pertinent portion of the video includes a synchronised transcript. Unfortunately, due to the press of time, I did not have the entire video transcribed. The first clip is approximately 30 seconds, and then I will switch to the second clip.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So we have to switch on to video. Press the video button.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Let us go back to your stay in Scheveningen, how will you organise your time there?" Interpreter's note: The sound is too poor to interpret.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I may, because the interpreters indicated the sound is poor, I will put on the synchronised transcript to assist the interpreter.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Tell me, you won't be watching television. Will you be using a computer? How will write those books? "I don't know that is possible. I have not yet been able to find that out. I have a laptop. "Journalist: That is good for communication, too. "Vojislav Seselj: One cannot communicate, the internet is certainly switched off. Whether it is possible to keep the laptop in the cell, without it being connected to the internet, that is another question. We will have to see that."

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: The point of the presentation, Your Honour, is to indicate that Professor Seselj should not be permitted to disable himself. If he wishes material in paper, he can simply push the print button and extract whatever material he wishes to have in paper format. We will, of course, provide a full response in writing upon receipt of his submission to disturb the prior Trial Chamber's order. I would note, however, that there is a disagreement regarding whether the propriety of electronic disclosure was conditioned by the prior Trial Chamber upon the presence of counsel to assist Professor Seselj. In fact, the decision was rendered at a point in time where Professor Seselj was representing himself, as now. The decision regarding counsel was later on -- several months later. So I don't think that that presents a good reason to require a change in circumstances. However, in formulating our response, we will be mindful of the volume of material that complying with his request would require and also the Chamber's indication of a preference for a subset of the material in paper form; for example, perhaps the exhibits. I believe that there is a way to find a middle ground that permits this case to be tried in an expeditious fashion and to avoid unnecessary delay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Dahl, you have produced an excerpt in which Mr. Seselj says that he can use a computer. He wants to write a book. But in writing a book and representing oneself in a trial, it's not quite the same thing. So in order to represent himself in these trial proceedings, normally speaking, he would need to know the 2.827 documents that are mentioned in the 65 ter list. He would need to know them in his language. And I think this is basically the gist of the decision that I will have to issue in hard copy as well. And although I was part of Trial Chamber II but I was not then the Pre-Trial Judge; therefore, I did not follow very closely the phase of disclosure of documents to Mr. Seselj. I do not know today which among the 2.827 documents the ones that he received directly and which documents went through the counsel that had been assigned to him. I do not know that, and you yourself may not know it either. But regardless of the 2.827 documents, there's another series of documents which you were bound to disclose to him under Rule 66 of the Rules. I have in mind the transcripts in which his name is mentioned, various testimonies or statements from other trial proceedings - Krajisnik, Milosevic, and other trial proceedings - in which he was involved. So that -- that represents quite a number of documents. And under Rule 68, he is also to be informed and receive all documents that might be exculpatory for him. So I'm not aware of the situation as such, and this situation has to be clarified. In order to do so, I'm going to give the floor -- or I'm going to invite Mr. Seselj, through his external associates, to help me so that I can issue a decision shortly; but supposing the decision is favourable to Mr. Seselj's case, what does this mean for the OTP? How much work does that represent for the OTP? I have another problem. If I were to find out that Mr. Seselj is going to be faced with a mountain of documents which is going -- which are going to be disclosed to him, if we want to have a fair -- for a fair hearing and under the principle of equality of arms, he's going to need quite some time to read them. And he's been waiting for his trial to begin for years. So this is the situation as it prevails today. I listened to you with great care. I watched the video excerpts, and I read between the lines. I have a feeling that you are still in the phase of electronic disclosure; it's easier for you but not at all easier for the accused. And I believe that you want to raise this issue again with the Appeals Chamber. So do you maintain that you want to disclose documents in electronic format?

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: I share the Chamber's concerns with getting this case ready for trial with affording Professor Seselj adequate time to prepare himself and the need to move forward. We will review his request and the burden that altering our obligations under the Rules and the practices of the Tribunal would present and report back to the Tribunal -- to the Chamber. With regard to the status of disclosure, we will not seek to rely on the fact of prior disclosure to the lawyer whom Professor Seselj rejected. We are prepared to re-disclose material out of an abundance of caution to ensure that he has the facilities for preparation of his Defence. That said, however, it cannot be permitted to allow Professor Seselj to disable himself and wilfully refuse to make available training and procedures that have been the foundation for the function of complex international criminal trials. Regarding the volume of material that is subject to disclosure under the Rules, I have three responses, conditioned of course on waiting for an opportunity to review and make a proper submission in writing to Professor Seselj's filing. The first is we are reviewing the exhibits and the witnesses to make sure that the case is narrowly tailored, that we present the most compelling evidence in the most concise format consistent with proving the allegations against the accused. Second, it may be that disclosure made in other cases that was tendered to Professor Seselj's then-counsel was over broad and not strictly required under the Rules. We will review the material to determine how best to satisfy our disclosure obligations. I appreciate the difficulty of large and complex cases; however, that is the nature of these proceedings. It is a large and complex case. And while Mr. Seselj may wish that the case against him was smaller, it remains the scope that it is and we will prove the allegations that have been made with the evidence that we have. He can elect to waive his right to review evidence that we have available for him in electronic format because he wishes to narrow his preparation to perhaps simply the exhibits that have been listed thus far or the expert reports and their annexes. The difficulties of self-representation are great and we will do what we can within the Rules and the procedures of this Tribunal and the orders of the Chamber to facilitate a fair trial and to make this happen in a timely basis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, Mr. Seselj, at this juncture I'm going to give you the floor. You have heard the senior trial attorney. I will need your filings very soon regarding disclosure in hard copy and in your language of all items under Rule 66 and under Rule 68, because this is the cornerstone of this trial. You explained that perfectly yourself. You have two positions. You can attend the trial proceeding as a spectator, without doing anything, without saying anything, because you would not have had the documents in your own language in hard copy; or, as you pointed out since I've been the Pre-Trial Judge, you do take part in the proceedings but making the demands that the Rules allow you to make. You have the floor back following what was said by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Antonetti, this morning when I saw an entirely new Prosecution team, I was glad, in the belief that Mrs. Retzlaff and Mr. Saxon were removed because of their lack of ability. I was beginning to believe that this new Prosecution team would be far more able. Unfortunately, I'm now disappointed having heard the new senior trial attorney. Unfortunately, I forget her name. I'm sure that with more time I will be able to memorize her name. I simply didn't write it down at the beginning of the Status Conference. I hope she doesn't take offence to this. But she keeps making the same mistakes as the previous OTP teams have already made. About two or three years ago, Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff insisted that documents should be delivered to me in English, saying that I knew English. Here in this courtroom, in much the same way, she showed footage of one of my interviews with a foreign journalist, a long time ago, in English, the simplest most basic possible kind of conversation or exchange. Let me see, 8, 12, 14, 16 years of education, well, one can only assume that I have learned enough English to exchange a couple of basic phrases with a journalist which still doesn't prove that I'm able to receive official documents in English. Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff made herself ridiculous in the courtroom, even the previous Pre-Trial Judge had to laugh when she showed that material. Now we have this new OTP team showing us this TV footage where I am on record as saying that I had a laptop; I did. I no longer have one. I even had two, but I lent them to my sons before I came to the Tribunal. You can't possibly think that I'm such an idiot as to not to be able to switch on a computer, connect to the internet or play some chess on my computer. I can type with all ten of my fingers. I have qualifications as a teleprinter in addition to all my other qualifications. You are twisting things around here. You are saying that I am refusing training. Yes, I'm refusing training. I am an inmate. It is not my duty to accept that I be trained. Had I not been trained earlier to take a shower early in the morning, to change my clothes every day, to wash my hands as often as I can every day, I don't think it would be you or your duty to train me now. You say one move on a computer is sufficient, I should just press a button and I can get all these documents on paper. Why don't you press that button? Why don't you make that move? Why don't you bring it to me on paper but that is not essential, is it. You know full well what the essence is. You want to disclose this material to me on DVD. You want me to hear the voice instead of reading the letter. You want testimony and evidence from other trials where transcripts have not yet been translated. You want to hand it to me in audio form, on tape, and for me to listen to it. My calculation is I would need 400 days to listen to it all, provided I listen to this material eight hours a day. I'm not falling into that trap. You have managed to make most of the lawyers defending people at this Tribunal fall into this trap. You want them to say they know English. It turns out, in the end, they have no idea about English. They looked at documents in English, they didn't even understand the first thing about those. All they cared about was making a killing. Many of them don't even listen to those tapes or to the transcripts. Well, I'm different. I want to go through it all. I need it on paper. I'm perfectly able to type on a typewriter using all ten of my fingers. Every time I wrote anything, even while I was still free before I was put in prison, I typed all of my pieces. I first wrote them and then typed them up. Well, I don't want to be involved in any of that. I don't want any tapes. I don't want to be driven mad by you. 400 days, eight hours per day, no one could possibly remain sane. When I get things on paper, I go through them pretty quickly. I just mark out what I believe is important and I leave out the rest, which is the essence really. When you get a tape, you can't do a selection and then it's even slowed down, this is courtroom time, and then people are being warned all the time to slow down because interpreters can't catch up, because people can't follow, and it's slow down, slow down all the time. I've looked at those; I know exactly what they're like. I cannot have you do this. I need it all on paper so that I can steadily prepare for the trial, and so that I can use paper copies to mark out the essential bits and leave out what I don't believe is important. I can use the margins to -- to put my comments there. I can't use a computer screen for something like that, can I? That is the essence of this problem and this something that you know full well. I'm not even sure why you showed this footage. I believe that you misused this Status Conference by showing that piece of footage; it is simply quite unbelievable. But I've seen that before, I've been through that before. Just because of those couple of phrases that I said in English once a long time ago; therefore, this doesn't particularly surprise me, to be brutally frank. But I can't have it. I simply will not accept this. I need everything on paper. I need everything in the Serbian language, and I am fully entitled to this. I'm entitled to this as an accused and as a human being. I want it all on paper. A document does not exist as long as there is no printed copy. You can film documents later on, which is something they did when I was heavily into science. It wasn't possible to scan documents back then, but still if you show a document to someone, you need to show a paper copy, a printed copy, and the same applies here. Instead of the OTP making it easier for me to prepare my defence, they keep requesting that I make it easy on them. How is that possible? This is what the bone of contention is here. You're still hoping that the Trial Chamber will eventually come along that will instruct me to receive everything in electronic form or in English. Maybe a Trial Chamber like that will come along, who knows, but nobody can make me do it. Nobody can force me to accept that. And I want no training. You want to train me in something that you would like to have me trained in. It is not in my interests. It's about you. I'm being told to go to the internet, but everything that was done on a computer was done on my behalf by the secretaries in my office. I've never done it myself. I won't do it now. I'll never need this for as long as I'm alive. Why would I make my days in prison any -- any bitterer than they are already? I'm not prepared to do that. Secondly, I identified your weakest link. You are falling into your own trap. You spent the last four years doing nothing. You are running out of time. You are saying, I'm hoping that you will curtail the number of witnesses or evidence or exhibits or amend the indictment again, whatever. All I'm hoping for is to beat you in this trial in a clear way. I will prove that your indictment is a false one, that your witnesses are false, that everything is false, and that I will simply walk away a free man. That's all I'm hoping for. When you extended the indictment, I didn't oppose that. Do you remember the transcript when we had a Status Conference here talking about your initiative, your application to have the indictment extended? I said, Please, make a list of all the war crimes that occurred anywhere in the former Yugoslavia, just in order to have this trial start as soon as possible, and then you can extend it or shorten it any which way you like. And then later on, you asked for me to be put in touch with Stanisic, Frenki Simatovic, Martic and Goran Hadzic. You've been manoeuvreing like that so frequently over the last four years, and then it turns out that there are only two witnesses that Martic and I have in common. What were you thinking about? That I should be left without a proper defence in a trial with multiple accused and then each have two counsel, and I am denied my fundamental rights as an accused just because there were no common points between the indictments. All these are things that you did, not me. You used these mechanisms. I was revolted by your behaviour and by your actions, that were against the law. I never did anything against the procedure and against the law and against the provisions. Now you end up facing a situation where you need more translators, you need to employ them. You need to put it all down on paper. You need to submit it all to me in Serbian because a document that is not a printed copy and that is not in Serbian, is a document that for me simply does not exist and never will.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, Mr. Seselj, you have explained something that you have been saying for several months, if not years, so this is of no surprise to me. Do send a request in writing as quickly as possible to me. We will have a reply by the Prosecution, and I will issue a decision. But you must have understood what my position was on this in the matter of disclosure. It is 10.30. For technical reasons we have to make a break, a 20-minute break, and we shall resume in 20 minutes' time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The hearing is resumed, following this 20-minute break. I shall proceed to deal with the problems we identified in the previous Status Conferences and today. Mr. Seselj, as I said last time, in the history of this Tribunal, this is the first time that an accused is representing himself. There was a precedent, it was Mr. Milosevic, but Milosevic had with him associates and a liaison officer who was the go-between between him, the Prosecution, and the registry. You do not at all intend to have this liaison officer, so that there can be no direct dialogue between the Prosecution and you; this dialogue goes through me, which is a further complication. Last time I dealt with the issue of Mrs. Regus, I shall come back to this, and I also spoke about your legal advisors. I can see already that when we have the actual trial proceedings in the active phase of these proceedings, you can remain alone, that's a fact, but last time I told you that it would be useful for you to have your associates close to you so that they can help you in various ways. First, they can check on the transcript, what has been translated into English, because there may be mistakes in the transcript, and whilst you're listening to me, whilst you're looking at the Prosecutor, and whilst you're watching the screen, you can't do everything. So no doubt you will need your assistants to help you in that. You also need them to be given documents. They can, if need be, provide you with information that may arise as a witness testifies. You will also need them to ask them to do some research because suddenly an idea might have crossed your mind, and since you're alone, you can't do everything. So I'd like to know the following: How do you plan whilst the trial is on to seek assistance? Did you decide to remain alone, on your own, or do you intend to have with you in the courtroom your assistants?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Antonetti, I would first just like to say two words in view of what you stated, that there are no direct contacts between myself and the Prosecution. There was this one contact. After the further initial appearance and the first Status Conference held on the same day, it was attended by Carla del Ponte, guards took me to Carla del Ponte's office. Carla del Ponte asked me whether I was prepared to talk to the Prosecutors. I said that I was prepared to talk on the condition that my legal advisors attend the meeting and that the entire conversation be recorded on video. After a while, I cannot remember how much time passed by, perhaps a month or two, I got a proposal in writing from the Office of the Prosecution -- Prosecutor to have this conversation take place; however, I had surgery, so I couldn't go through with this. But then I got another offer from them later, saying that we can have a meeting without my legal advisors present and then they said that perhaps one could attend but not more than one. I wasn't the one who avoided these contacts. It was the Prosecution that avoided these contacts. I thought that even in that stage, when talking to them, we could have done away with a lot of the counts in the indictment, the false statements, the false witnesses, and so on and so forth. This would have saved a lot of time for them as well, the OTP, but they didn't want to do it; they shied away from that. I never evaded any meetings with the registry. However, I don't want to have a liaison officer of mine who would be their officer. That is what I find unacceptable a priori. However, whoever the registry send to me to talk to me, I would invariably receive them and I never refused to talk to them; that will be the case in the future as well. However, I do not accept that some official from the registry be a go-between, between myself and the Prosecution. No. If the Prosecution wants to see me outside the courtroom, they can. My legal advisors, the head of the investigation team, the case manager, and so on, they can bring as many officials as they want. We can discuss anything. But they are running away from that. It seems that they are sort of afraid of that. Secondly, as far as the trial itself is concerned, you remember, Mr. Antonetti, that I repeated my insistence that I should sit in the first row of these seats that are for the Defence so that visually I would be on a footing of equality in respect of the Office of the Prosecutor; that is important for the Prosecution witnesses who will appear here. It is also important for Defence witnesses so that they would not be intimidated. I don't want to seem as if I were a little mouse sitting in the back of the gallery and the Prosecutors would be dominating the room. I think that my legal advisor and case manager should be in the courtroom all the time; however, they cannot do that until the question of financing my defence is resolved. The registry has been avoiding this issue all the time. They have constantly been refusing my requests. So far the only thing they accepted is to pay 1500 euro to the project leader which is not enough for living in The Hague. And also 1200 euro for an apartment where the legal advisors would live, as if they were doing some kind of a service to me. I asked for them to pay for this apartment so they wouldn't pay for hotels and it's easier for all the documents to be in one place and they would be in one place, too, so they could go home together and so on and so forth. This, as a matter of fact, cut the expenses of the defence and the obligations of the registry; however, the registry has refused this. Until the question of the Defence is resolved, it is impossible for my legal advisors to sit here with me in the courtroom. Because they have to live on something. They have to make a living, they have to support their families. They have to give up on their other professional commitments in Belgrade as members of parliament and they have to devote themselves exclusively to matters related to my defence. I said to the representative of the registry, the last time it was John Hocking, the Deputy Registrar, I said to him that we can find a simple solution. What is the monthly salary of lead counsel and co-counsel in another case, and then if that sum can be divided into three that can be the salary for my legal advisors. I'm prepared to participate, in part, in the costs of my defence in line with the money I have. Of course I cannot use my frozen assets and I shall certainly not engage an American lawyer. I am actually negotiating with an American lawyer in order to take to court in New York, the United Nations, not even the Tribunal. So perhaps for that I could retain a US attorney for maltreatment, the hunger strike, and so on and so forth. But hurry-up then. Have this money transferred to me because I am going to transfer that money straight away to that lawyer in New York and then I won't have any money left. I can sacrifice that money, but I cannot give in to an ultimatum to retain a US lawyer here. Secondly, I have had enormous expenses over these past four years and I owe a great deal of money to my legal advisors and to the members of the expert team for assisting the Defence. They have already threaten me twice in writing that they would stop working on my defence if I did not pay them and I have no means for that. The Statute guaranties resources for my defence. Resources are primarily money. Money is the equivalent of all resources. It is the equivalent of the value of the legal advisors and the technical work needed and translations and photocopies and what have you not. The registry is still refusing this. I complained a few times to the President of the Tribunal about the registry, and every time the President of the Tribunal told me that this was up to the Trial Chamber. So it is up to you, Mr. Antonetti, and your colleagues to decide on this matter. I have exhausted all my possibilities. It is pointless for me to go on writing to the registry on this particular subject. The registry has particularly avoided providing me with information on what the costs were of the Defence in all other cases that were financed from the budget of the United Nations, or rather, the budget of this Tribunal. This information has to be made public. The money of the UN has to be spent publicly and cannot be kept away from the eyes of the public. Also, I asked for information to be provided to me what the cost was for the UN of the stand-by counsel, the imposed counsel, the members of their teams. There were two teams, Hooper's and Van der Spoel's. Also they denied me this information. I also asked for information to be submitted to me as to what the costs of the Prosecution were in my case so far and I didn't receive that information either. This information is indispensable in order to see what the expenses for my Defence would be in an impartial ways. Of course those costs and expenses will be lower than the costs of other cases and of the Prosecutor because I'm representing myself and I have already given up on my own fee to benefit this court. So my work doesn't have to be paid for, but the work of all other persons has to be paid for. I'm prepared to participate in payments for their work but with the money that I have available and every day I have less and less money. I have this other bank account in Canada, and I withdrew money from there and I was prepared to invest it in my Defence; however, I had to spend this money on supporting my family as this went on for four years. What could I do? It was half the amount or even less than what is on the account in New York and I still have the so-called old foreign-exchange earnings in Belgrade. You probably don't even understand what this is. All our savings from the communist period are frozen and are paid in very small amounts every year, and this will go on until 2017 or whatever. I had a car as well. In the meantime, my family sold this car so that they could live off that too and then there is nothing. The court has to pay for everything else. The court doesn't have money -- It's not my fault that the court doesn't have enough money. The registry has less and less money; it's not my fault. Why are there -- why are your sponsors not responsive? Why don't they pay you money or why doesn't somebody else pay you money? These are problems that the court has to resolve, the registry, not me. But without resolving the problems of financing the Defence, my legal advisors cannot stay in The Hague, they cannot be present in the courtroom, and they cannot fully dedicate themselves to working on my case. What they did so far, they did parallel to all their other duties. This was a work of lesser importance for them. They practically did all of this by way of a hobby and they did a great deal of work at that. In terms of quality, they did a better job than the Prosecution. In terms of quantity, we cannot even compare. You may object and say that I have too many submissions, but if you look at all my submissions made to the Court and if you look at all the pages submitted by the Prosecution, you will see that there is this enormous advantage on the side of the OTP. They produced a lot more material and distributed it to various addresses, at that. So there is this problem of financing that has to be resolved. Mr. Antonetti, when your Trial Chamber deals with that, then I will definitely give you an answer as to whether I'm going to be alone in this courtroom or not. If the problem is not resolved in line with the Statute, I will certainly be in the courtroom on my own.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, very well. You listed a series of problems in your answer. I shall endeavour to resolve these problems. The first problem is that you filed an application in order to be in a position like the Prosecution in the first line. You consider that you should not be at the bottom of the hall. You told me last time, but we discussed other subjects and I hadn't discussed it with the registry but I am going soon to discuss it with the registry. Now, on this question at this stage I have to tell you this because I too, I had considered, estimated, that the accused should be ready, should be close, should be close to their counsel, indeed, and the registry at the time in another trial had let me know that for security reasons it was not possible. I did not quite understand the security reasons. I don't think you are going to assault me or assault anybody here, nor any witness, nor Madam Prosecutor or her assistants. So I did not very well understand the position of the registry on this score. In my country, the accused are close to the Judges, in presence of their counsel. Lately I have seen in the United States a trial concerning a terrorist who was seated a few yards from the Judge who was presiding at the hearing. So I -- what I was told needs to be explicited [as interpreted] and I will discuss the matter with the Registrar. And I will see to it that you would be as close as possible. I think it is obvious, but perhaps for others it is nonsensical. Therefore, this matter is going to be examined by myself and the registry. You also said that on your side, for your part, you would be in favour of having your associates in the room and you also mentioned about the problem of remuneration for these assistants. It is on the agenda and I am immediately going to review it. Last time I spoke with the Registrar on this topic and I invited the registry to seize the legal advisor of United Nations of this problem, this problem for the Defence of an accused. Because as you know, if the Rules has provided for this help for the counsel, nothing has been provided for the case where an accused is defending himself. The only precedent was in the Milosevic case where Mr. Milosevic had some associates, some liaison officers, and this was therefore -- there was a process put in place by the registry in order to remunerate the people in question. But for the moment this question is not solved. So the goal for the Pre-Trial Judge is to identify what are the problems which are hindering the beginning of a trial. I now have spoken about the electronic disclosure and the documents. That is a major problem and I'm going to solve it. A second problem is the question of your associates or legal advisors, which I think is also an important problem. I have seen that on a document you indicated that you have 25 associates or legal advisors and I wondered whether these 25 individuals were working for you gratis or whether those are people which you are trying to indemnify as much as possible. I thought I understood, in your answers, that you have to pay certain expenses to the members of this team. This is what I understood from what your -- what you said, and if I didn't understand you rightly, please tell me later. Among the 25 individuals, we have their names on different documents, I do not know this or that person. It starts by Mr. Tomislav Nikolic, and it finishes by Mrs. Marina Toman, Jerkovic, Vucic, Todorovic, Krasic, Radeta, Radovanovic, Bozic-Talijan, Maric, Vukovic, Nadoveza, Sarovic, Terzic, Migati, Blagojevic, Jojic, Zobenica, Savic, Stojanovic, Mihajlovic, Marina Ragus, Momir Markovic, and Mihajlovic, Marina Toman. Among all these individuals, I thought there might be either law teachers or counsel or jurists or students, law students. Could you give me at your own level, although you have no obligation to do so, who they are? I'm just inviting you to tell me if among the experts for your Defence there are some law professors, students or jurists, and so on. Could you tell me?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Antonetti. My expert team consists of 25 persons. I have been disclosing their names all the time on my submissions. I submitted a separate submission to the registry, acquainting them with the fact that these are going to be persons who will in a way be made aware of confidential material, and that they are duty-bound to preserve that confidentiality. My expert teams consists of two parts: A legal team and a team of investigators. The legal team consists of two lawyers. Nemanja Sarovic is their assistant, and Zoran Krasic, Aleksandar Vucic, and a few others who have degrees in law. For me, they carry out legal work. First of all, they write submissions in accordance with my instructions. Investigators work in the field. I believe that my case before this Tribunal is perhaps the most complicated one, not only in terms of the fact that a new crime was invented, rather, the commission of a crime through hate speech which never existed in international law before, but also because my alleged crimes are spread through the territory of three states. After the Slobodan Milosevic case, there is not a single case in which the alleged crimes of the accused person involved were committed in such a widespread fashion. That calls for a larger number of investigators, especially because I had not heard of some of these crimes before I saw them in the indictments. For example, Borah in Herzegovina, Lipovaca or Lipovica, whatever its name is, and so on. That is why I need a larger number of investigators. I have given them specific locations. I am not asking for a monthly salary to be paid to all members of my expert team. What I'm asking for is that a budget be set for the Defence, because of the complexity of this case, in the pre-trial stage and also in the trial stage, that is called the Prosecution case, then also in the trial stage when I present my own case and call my own witnesses, and of course in the appeals stage. Because that is what the registry has done in other cases, too. Then some of my legal advisors would allocate that money, depending on the efforts made by individuals aimed at my defence, it would be Mr. Zoran Krasic. You find his name on most of the documents that I have been sending to you, that is the man who did most of the work together with me on my defence until now. I'm not asking for a salary for all, but have a budget set for the Defence. The pre-trial stage on the basis of such, such, and such indicators is worth this much, I can pay this much, the registry has to pay the rest. So it's the language of numbers. All of this can be established through very precise methods. And in order to do that, we have to have comparative information from other cases, otherwise it is undoable. Therefore, I ask you not to be confused by the number of members of this team. For example, on this team I have typists as well. I have people who are engaged in technical matters, who are looking for different books and newspapers in libraries, for instance, and so on and so forth. So this is a wide range of people that I have engaged. Everyone has a role of their own. For example, Tomislav Nikolic is carrying out work on my behalf before the bar of the Netherlands, the bar of England, where I initiated proceedings against the stand-by lawyer, the imposed lawyer, and then within that team he also communicates on my behalf with the European court for human rights, the committee for human rights of the United Nations. He writes to the Security Council. He also writes to other associations that deal with human rights. He is in contact with foreign diplomats and so on and so forth. Everyone has a role of his own, but I am in charge of all of that from here, from The Hague, and I am not asking - and I repeat this - that every one of them be paid a salary. Let a budget be set for the Defence, and then the lead Defence advisor would allocate those resources, depending on the needs involved.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for these specifications which will enable to progress and better understand the problems we have at hand. In your team of 25 individuals, there's a distinction to be made between the jurists, those who draft the applications, and you mentioned Mr. Zoran Krasic and one also -- the names we see in the motions. You spoke of Mr. Tomislav Nikolic, who is your representative for the -- for several institutions, but in particular - and this caught my attention - I had seen up to now, you indicated that there were also people who were performing investigations on -- in the field and to prepare the witnesses which you will call when you will present your own evidence. And I think the Statute is very clear on this. You should have the facilities for -- within the principle of the equality of arms. So, therefore, these people, even if you defend yourself alone, these people have to be paid. So there -- again, there is a real problem, and I am going to seize the registry of this problem. And you said, rightly so, a while ago that each time you asked the registry, you appealed to the President of the Tribunal, who sent you back to the Chamber - and you're perfectly right - anything which can obstruct or hinder the exercise of the rights of the Defence is within the competence and jurisdiction of the Chamber. And here you have indeed presented a real problem, which is the retribution of those who perform inquiries for you within the framework of your Defence, investigators, I mean, the counsel represent the accused, and there is a certain global sum which is provided for so that counsel can then pay their investigators or experts. Now, in this case we are in another framework, another system, and for the moment we see that there is a legal void, vacuum, a legal vacuum which has to be made good, and I'm going to look at this problem with the registry to solve these questions. We're going to have a working meeting on this question, and you can count on me to see that matters will go forward, because here again this is an element which might hinder good proceedings of this trial, and this is a very important element for what is provided by the Statute, which is that you should have the facilities which are necessary for your Defence. Since we also have to review the question of the assistants and of Mrs. Regus, it is true that personally, just like you, I consider that what has been provided for is really very -- a very small sum, 1.500 euro for Mrs. Regus and 1.200 for an apartment, which should shelter four people. And that this is not within 1.200 euros that you can find an apartment or a flat which could have four people. So we have here a real problem, and I'm going to discuss it again with the registry. A while ago when I spoke of a liaison officer, perhaps we didn't understand each other. The term "liaison officer," I get the feeling that on your side, you are diffidence of the idea of a liaison officer who would be appointed by the registry and who would be an agent of the registry. Right? So, Mr. Seselj, I have to tell you that for the last three years I've been here, I can certify to you that the registry is really worthy of all praise, and they are perfectly neutral towards anybody. The registry has no bias at all, neither for the Prosecution nor -- even less for the accused. And if they wanted to designate a liaison officer, you have to know that the person who would have this task would not be an agent, an informant, somebody in the hand of the Registrar or the Prosecution or the Chamber. It would really be someone independent, as are all the civil servants of this registry with whom I had the honour to meet and to discuss with. They are people who are very praise-worthy and who discharge very well their mission under the Statute and the Rules. But if there is a real block, which I could understand for psychological reasons or subjective reasons, there might be another solution which would be to have you designate that person who would play the role of a go-between between the registry and the Prosecution and the Chamber, an interface in this case. I'm proposing this for you to think about. I'm going to talk to the registry to see if there's a feasibility of designating, without talking about Mrs. Regus or the three assistants, somebody else who could be your spokesman, spokesperson, and who would play this role between the registry, the Prosecution [as interpreted], and yourself. But this person will have to do so against retribution. Of course, not free of charge, not gratis. So there I'm going to be obliged to examine this question very soon with the registry to see if it's possible financially to have this agent, liaison officer, appointed, which brings me to talk about the situation of Mrs. Marina Regus, who still hasn't been paid and who normally would be your case manager, as they say here in English. I know that you had entrusted her to the registry, who was supposed to examine and give an agreement and so on. Personally, I see only advantages the fact that this lady may be as soon as possible in The Hague -- may come as soon as possible in The Hague and help you in your work in the contacts which she will have with you, if need be. At this stage, this is what I'm telling you now, this means meetings with the registrar, between me and the Registrar, to try and go forward to make some headway because if you defend yourself, it doesn't mean - I'm going to give you the floor - that you have to do everything from A to Z. You will, of course, have to be helped in your several tasks. I am now giving you the floor, Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: To the court reporters, replace "Prosecution" by "administration" the last time it was said about the interpreter.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- would be my case manager and she's ready to travel to The Hague as soon as a salary is determined for her, which would be a minimum salary compared to her education. She is a political scientist, a graduate of the Faculty of Political Sciences, and she's proficient in English. She must be paid in accordance with her qualifications. 1.500 euros is a minimum salary within the ICTY, according to my information. This is humiliating for a case manager, and you know perfectly well that one cannot survive in the Hague on that sort of salary. Secondly, I have very good objective reasons for my diffidence towards the registry and I will name just one, Mr. Antonetti. Late in 2003 and in the first half of 2004, for a full seven months I was forbidden to use the phone at all or receive visits, including visits by my family. I was barred from any contact with the outside world. Do you know how that was explained? The first information was I would have had a way of influencing good election results for my party, the Serb Radical Party, and the second explanation was I had previously been known to get in touch with journalists.
